bull.b: The PIPE financing and licensing proceeds materially extend Jasper’s ability to fund research and clinical milestones without immediately relying on another raise. A runway through the second half of 2028 provides greater planning stability while the enlarged pipeline advances toward important regulatory and clinical catalysts.

Acquiring Kira broadens Jasper from a single primary development focus into a more diversified immunology pipeline with multiple clinical and regulatory milestones. Several programs at different development stages can improve the company’s opportunity set and reduce dependence on one asset’s outcome.

The Mirador agreement provides immediate upfront funding while allowing an external partner to develop the C5a-targeting assets. Retaining potential milestone economics creates additional value optionality and can support Jasper’s capital base without requiring all development spending to remain internal.

bear.b: Jasper has no commercial product revenue to offset its research and operating expenses, so financial performance remains dependent on pipeline progress rather than an established sales base. Persistent losses mean profitability and operating leverage are not yet visible, increasing execution dependence over the next several quarters.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow requires Jasper to preserve liquidity and secure external capital while advancing clinical programs. Although TTM burn improved from 2025, continued funding dependence can constrain development choices and expose shareholders to financing risk if milestones take longer or cost more.

The transaction substantially reduced existing Jasper holders’ economic ownership as Kira shareholders and PIPE investors received most of the enlarged company. This changes the shareholder base and limits legacy holders’ participation in future upside, while preferred-stock conversion could further increase common-share supply.
